title: Louis Jordan and his father, and Louis's cutting contest with Lester in 1924
summary: Jordan's father led the Rabbit Foot show band; young Louis Jordan on soprano met the Young show and battled Lester on Running Wild and the blues.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: During that time, you played with Louis Jordan.
You might want to go back now and talk about his father, and also the jam session or cutting contest of whatever that he had with Lester Young.
First of all, tell us about his father and tell us about anything you know about him. Your brother, Clarence, played with him, too.

That's right. Well, his father used to have the bands on those shows, like minstrel shows. He had a band on a show called Rabbit Foots, and Louis was in that band. But Louis was playing clarinet then. He was a pretty good clarinet player, too, you know. He was playing clarinet. He was young then. He was in short pants, too. His father was a helluva musician, too. Then he put the clarinet down and started playing the soprano sax. That's what he and Les was battlin' with.
What year was this? This was when you were with the family show?
That must have been in 1925, something like that. Or 1924. When I first got with them.
So this was when you were on the first tour.
No, it was a little later than that. It must have been April.
So we met up with them. Louis was playing with a little dance band, and we met up with him, and he and Les got to playing and they got to battling with each other.
What pieces were they playing on?
